title: Miso Soup
subtitle: Japanese dashi broth with miso, tofu, and wakame
excerpt: The simplest and most daily of Japanese soups: a light, clear broth made from kombu and bonito flakes, dissolved with white miso, and served with cubes of silken tofu and rehydrated wakame seaweed. Ready in ten minutes.

recipe.sourceNotes: Miso soup (miso shiru) is the daily soup of Japanese domestic cooking, eaten at breakfast, lunch, and dinner, often multiple times a day. It is built on dashi, the fundamental stock of Japanese cooking, made from kombu (dried kelp) and katsuobushi (dried bonito flakes). The dashi provides the umami base; the miso provides body and flavour. White miso (shiro miso) is the mildest and sweetest, made with a higher proportion of rice koji; red miso (aka miso) is stronger and saltier. Miso soup varies by household and region: the additions — tofu, wakame, daikon, spring onion, clams — are chosen to match the season and what is available. The critical technique is that miso must never boil after it is dissolved into the soup; boiling destroys the delicate enzymes and flattens the flavour.

content.text: Never boil miso: add it off the heat or at the very end over the lowest possible heat. Boiling kills the flavour enzymes and flattens the soup. Make the dashi first and keep it at a gentle simmer. Whisk the miso with a little of the warm dashi before adding it to the pot to prevent lumps.

items.preparation: 1 piece, about 10 x 10 cm; wiped with a damp cloth, do not rinse
or a mix of white and red miso
dried; soaked in cold water for 5 minutes, drained and squeezed

content.text: Make the dashi: put the kombu in a medium saucepan with 1 litre of cold water. Bring very slowly to just below a simmer over low heat, about 10 minutes. Remove the kombu just before the water boils. Increase the heat until the water comes to a simmer, add the bonito flakes, and immediately remove from the heat. Leave to steep for 3 minutes, then strain. The dashi should be pale golden.

Return the dashi to the pan over low heat. Whisk the miso with 4 tablespoons of the warm dashi in a small bowl until smooth. Add the tofu cubes and wakame to the dashi and heat gently until the tofu is warmed through. Do not boil.
Remove from the heat and stir in the dissolved miso. Taste: the soup should be gently savoury and warming, not aggressively salty. Ladle into bowls and scatter with spring onion. Serve immediately.
